thread:
maria: Heads up — after the merge that landed earlier (PR #4321) we're seeing ~2x p99 on long-context workloads in canary. Suspect kernel prefetch or selector change. Rollout paused :hand:
kevin: ugh, saw the alert. Can you paste the perf numbers and the exact canary commit?
sam: repro steps are short: checkout canary image sha `sha256:abc123`, run perf harness with seq_len=4096 and batch=1. p50 ~120ms, p99 jumped from ~420ms -> ~900ms. Quick paste from harness:
```
seq_len=4096 batch=1 tokens=4096 p50=120ms p95=480ms p99=910ms
cpu% spike on kernel_selector_main thread
```
jia: attaching flame snippet (upload in #eng-runtime-artifacts). Looks like a new branch in kernel selection is frequently choosing the prefetch path which ends up doing an extra memcpy on long prefixes. Not purely batching.
ci-bot: Perf check failed on latest merge: `benchmark/latency/long-context` regression +92% (threshold 20%). Full CI link: https://ci.example.company/12345
maria: ok can someone run a quick git-bisect? My hunch is the selector heuristic change in 6df4c9 but want data.
kevin: I'll start a bisect run but we need an automated test binary to exit non-zero on regression. Sam — can your harness return code 1 when p99 > 700ms?
sam: yep. I'll push a small wrapper `tools/perf_gate.sh`:
```
#!/bin/bash
# usage: perf_gate.sh <bin>
./$1 --seq=4096 --batch=1 --warmup=3 --runs=5 | tee out.txt
p99=$(tail -n1 out.txt | awk '{print $NF}')
if (( $(echo "$p99 > 700" | bc -l) )); then exit 1; else exit 0; fi
```
kevin: perfect. running `git bisect start --term-old=good --term-new=bad` then `git bisect run ./tools/perf_gate.sh bazel-bin/runtime/server_perf_test`
jia: note — the selector has a config flag `--selector-prefetch-threshold` that was defaulted to 1.5x in that PR. If bisect points there we can hotfix by reverting the flag change rather than the whole PR.
maria: run started. I'll leave it overnight. @deploy-bot do not promote canary further until we have a revert or mitigation.
deploy-bot: Canary promotion paused by user request from @maria.
kevin: update: bisect narrowed to commit `6df4c9b` -> `a2b8e47` range, current candidate `8c9f1d2` which touches kernel selector and alloc paths. Running local repro now.
sam: while that's running, I instrumented KV cache hit stats. On the bad commit we see a 30% increase in cache misses (prefix mismatches) — could be selector reordering keys? log snippet:
```
KV cache: hits=7034 misses=3012 hit_rate=70.1%
KV cache (bad): hits=5100 misses=4820 hit_rate=51.4%
```
jia: if selector changed the order of ops we might be invalidating prefetches or shifting alignment so KV keys don't match the cache lookup windows. Weird but plausible.
maria: kevin — any chance to reproduce in CI runner image? If local repro depends on dev machine kernels it won't help.
kevin: bisect run reproduced in our Linux perf runner VM. Found failing commit: `8c9f1d2` (author: @thor). It adds a new prefetch stage and tweaks selector heuristics.
sam: I ran a quick patch reverting the prefetch call in `prefetch_manager.cpp` and rebench: p99 back to ~430ms. Patch small.
kevin: can you open a revert PR for just the prefetch invocation and tag it as rollback-candidate? We'll run canary with that.
jia: also add a config flag to gate the selector change so we can ship the rest of the PR safely. Two-step: revert prefetch, add `--enable-selector-prefetch` default false.
maria: agreed. Action items:
- sam: open rollback PR that removes prefetch invocation and adds a config flag (assign to kevin for review)
- kevin: run canary with rollback and performance harness, post numbers here
- jia: prepare short postmortem blurb explaining why KV cache miss rate jumped (for incidents)
- ci-bot: once rollback PR lands, run full perf-suite and block promotion if fail persists

sam: filing PR now: https://git.example.company/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/987 (WIP)

kevin: initial canary with revert applied looks good: p99=440ms p95=480ms p50=130ms. KV hit_rate back to ~69%
maria: nice. I'll approve the rollback PR after kevin's final run. Waiting 30m to watch for noise. :thumbsup:
jia: for long-term, I'll add a regression test in our perf suite that exercises KV alignment + selector heuristics so this doesn't slip.
kevin: learned: big heuristics changes should be feature-flagged in the same PR. Lesson for code review.
ci-bot: Perf suite run queued for PR 987.

maria: thanks all — closing the immediate rollback loop. Follow-up: retro next Tue.
